correctness.rationale: The cited Cerulli Irelli–Feigin–Reineke smooth-locus Poincaré polynomial is q^{n(n-1)/2} times the standard Schröder diagonal-count polynomial. Removing k diagonals gives a Dyck path of semilength n-k and stars-and-bars reinsertion into 2(n-k)+1 slots, hence a[n,k]=binom(2n-k,k)C[n-k]. The quotient a[n,k+1]/a[n,k]=(n-k)(n-k+1)/((k+1)(2n-k)); difference after clearing the positive denominator is 2k^2-4nk+n^2-n, crossing at rho=n-sqrt(n(n+1)/2). Its sole integer zero yields consecutive equal maxima iff n(n+1)/2=s^2 iff (2n+1)^2-8s^2=1. Independently checked all coefficient rows/mode positions for n<=120, yielding Pell plateaus n=1,8,49; finite examples corroborate but the symbolic ratio is the general proof. Grading shift n(n-1)/2 is carried unchanged.
